# Hypertorus Fusion Reactor
The Hypertorus Fusion Reactor (HFR) is a 3x3 multiblock engine that fuses a hot fuel mix into power and exotic gases. It is the most demanding machine on the ship: it needs a fuel feed, a moderator feed, a coolant loop and a waste line, and it cannot be turned off safely once the reaction is running.
## Buying one
The crate is sold by cargo under **Atmospherics** for **10,000 credits**. It contains the core, the console, the three side parts, four corners and a printed quick guide. The HFR is not lathe-printable and does not spawn on ships by default.
## Assembly
Lay the parts out as a 3x3 block, with the **core in the centre**: - four [bold]corners[/bold] on the diagonal tiles, - the **fuel input**, **moderator input** and **waste output** on three of the cardinal tiles, - the **console** on the remaining cardinal tile next to the core.
Anchor every part. The core will not accept the console or the side parts until they are anchored in the right pattern; a wrench is enough. When the pattern is complete the console links itself to the core and its power draw switches on.
## Piping and wiring
- **Coolant loop**: the core's south port. Feed it cold plasma or hyper-noblium and dump the return into space or a heat exchanger. The loop is what keeps the core from melting. - **Fuel input**: the fuel mix (most recipes use tritium, hydrogen, plasma or oxygen). - **Moderator input**: the moderator gas. Hyper-noblium lowers the reaction power, anti-noblium raises it. - **Waste output**: the fusion products. At power level 5 and above the console refuses to dump waste, so give it a real line. - The console needs **Engineering access** and an LV power connection (it draws 350 W idle and about 100 kW while the reaction runs).
## Operation
1. Open the console and pick a **recipe** in the recipe table. The table shows the fuel pair, the products and the multipliers so you can compare recipes before starting. 2. Set the **fuel input rate** and **moderator input rate** (0.1–150 mol/s). 3. Press **Start Cooling**, then **Start Power**. The console will report the fusion temperature, efficiency, instability and the current power level. 4. At level 1, drop the **Heating Conductor** from its starting 500 to about 100. If the temperature keeps climbing, raise the **Current Damper** and the **Magnetic Constrictor**. 5. The reaction only starts once the fuel mix is hot enough. A 50/50 tritium/hydrogen mix of roughly 2000 mol, with only about 1000 mol let into the core at first, is the standard kickstart.
## Recipes
- Plasma + Oxygen - Hydrogen + Oxygen - Tritium + Oxygen - Hydrogen + Tritium - Hyper-Noblium + Hydrogen - Hyper-Noblium + Tritium - Hyper-Noblium + Anti-Noblium
## Failure
If the core overheats it will melt down: a large explosion, an EMP, spreading fire and a radiation pulse. The console shows the instability and the time left; use the **filter gases** controls to strip helium and anti-noblium from the fusion mix, or flood the moderator loop with hyper-noblium to bring the power down.
The reactor cannot be dismantled or powered off while its power level is above 0. If the APC dies, the fusion keeps running but the coolant stops — fix the power before the temperature reaches the melting point.
